q-63544.name: Question 1
q-63544.problem:
Which of the following values of $v$ satisfy the inequality $7v\le 28\,?$

I. $v=1$

II. $v=3$

III. $v=4$
q-63544.worked_solution:
We substitute each value into the given inequality and check to see if the resulting statement is true or false.

- We substitute the value $v=1$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}7v & \le 28 \\ 7\cdot 1 & \le 28 \\ 7 & \le 28\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $v=1$ into the inequality leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $v=1$ **satisfies** this inequality.

- We substitute the value $v=3$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}7v & \le 28 \\ 7\cdot 3 & \le 28 \\ 21 & \le 28\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $v=3$ into the inequality leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $v=3$ **satisfies** this inequality.

- We substitute the value $v=4$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}7v & \le 28 \\ 7\cdot 4 & \le 28 \\ 28 & \le 28\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $v=4$ into the inequality leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $v=4$ **satisfies** this inequality.

q-64151.name: Question 7
q-64151.problem:
Which of the following values of $a$ satisfy the inequality $-3\le 2a+1<8\,?$

I. $a=-2$

II. $a=2$

III. $a=5$
q-64151.worked_solution:
We substitute each value into the given inequality and check to see if the resulting statement is true or false.

- We substitute the value $a=-2$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3\le 2a+1 & <8 \\ -3\le 2\cdot (-2)+1 & <8 \\ -3\le -3 & <8\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $a=-2$ into the inequality leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $a=-2$ **satisfies** this inequality.

- We substitute the value $a=2$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3\le 2a+1 & <8 \\ -3\le 2\cdot 2+1 & <8 \\ -3\le 5 & <8\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $a=2$ into the inequality leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $a=2$ **satisfies** this inequality.

- We substitute the value $a=5$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3\le 2a+1 & <8 \\ -3\le 2\cdot 5+1 & <8 \\ -3\le 11 & <8\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $a=5$ into the inequality leads to a **false** statement. 

Therefore, $a=5$ **does not satisfy** this inequality.

q-101923.name: Question 8
q-101923.problem:
The value $z=0$ satisfies which of the following inequalities?

I. $z+3\ge 1$

II. $3z+1<0$

III. $-6\le \frac{z}{2}-1\le -2$
q-101923.worked_solution:
We substitute the given value into each of the inequalities and check to see if the resulting statement is true or false.

- We substitute the value $z=0$ into the first inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}z+3 & \ge 1 \\ 0+3 & \ge 1 \\ 3 & \ge 1\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $z=0$ leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $z=0$ **satisfies** this inequality.

- We substitute the value $z=0$ into the second inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}3z+1 & <0 \\ 3\cdot 0+1 & <0 \\ 1 & <0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $z=0$ leads to a **false** statement. 

Therefore, $z=0$ **does not satisfy** this inequality.

- We substitute the value $z=0$ into the third inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}-6\le \frac{z}{2}-1 & \le -2 \\ -6\le \frac{0}{2}-1 & \le -2 \\ -6\le -1 & \le -2\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $z=0$ leads to a **false** statement.  

Therefore, $z=0$ **does not satisfy** this inequality.

So, substituting $y=-1$ leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $y=-1$ **satisfies** this inequality.

Therefore, $x=4$ ** does not satisfy** this inequality.
